mainTopic: Rules for dissolving vows, the sin of vowing, and the wording a husband and a חכם must use to remove vows
overview: This amud opens by finishing a report of a vow dissolved in a side room of the study hall, standing, by one person, at night. רבה quotes רב נחמן's ruling: vows may be dissolved standing, by a single expert, at night, on שבת, and by relatives, even if there was time before שבת. The גמרא challenges the 'standing' part from a ברייתא where רבן גמליאל got off his donkey and sat down to dissolve a vow. It answers that רבן גמליאל holds פותחין בחרטה, which needs careful examination, while רב נחמן does not. רבא then reports that the רבנן in ארץ ישראל told someone whose vow they dissolved to pray for mercy, because anyone who vows is called a sinner, as רב זביד learns from a פסוק. Next, a ברייתא lists which words of a husband do nothing and which confirm his wife's vow. It also teaches how he cancels her vow on שבת, with רבי יוחנן adding that he must cancel it in his heart, and בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about cancelling in the heart. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules that a חכם and a husband cannot use each other's wording. A ברייתא begins to prove from "זה הדבר" that a husband cannot release vows, and the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where and how the vow was dissolved
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier report: the vow was dissolved in a side room of the study hall, standing, by one person, at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a side room of the study hall, standing, alone, and at night.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a report that started before this section, telling us the conditions under which a vow was dissolved. It sets up the הלכה that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each detail matters. 'Standing' means the חכם didn't sit like a judge, 'alone' means one person and not a בית דין of three, and 'at night' means it wasn't during court hours. The next step turns these exact details into a ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Alone, one person (not a בית דין of three)

phrases.english: In a side room of the study hall,
standing, alone, and at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes a report begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow was dissolved standing, by one person, at night, in a side room.

steps.title: רב נחמן's ruling on dissolving vows
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes רב נחמן: vows may be dissolved standing, alone, at night, on שבת, and by relatives, even if there was time before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רב נחמן: The הלכה is that one may ask to have vows dissolved standing, alone, at night, on שבת, and before relatives, even if they had free time while it was still day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה reports רב נחמן's practical ruling, which makes dissolving vows very flexible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dissolving a vow is not treated like a full court case, so the usual court rules (sitting, three judges, daytime, no relatives) don't apply. It may even be done on שבת by someone who could have done it before שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: We may ask a חכם to dissolve vows
While it was still day (before שבת began)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה for התרת נדרים, and the rest of the section tests it.

phrases.english: Rabba said that Rav Naḥman said:
The law is: vows may be asked about (to dissolve them)
standing, alone, and at night,
phrases.notes: 'Alone' means one expert is enough; you don't need a court of three.

phrases.english: and on Shabbat, and by relatives,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָיָה לָהֶן פְּנַאי מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם.
phrases.english: and even if they had free time while it was still day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the report's conditions into a general ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vows may be dissolved standing, by one expert, at night, on שבת, and by relatives, even if it could have been done earlier.

steps.title: Challenge: רבן גמליאל sat down to dissolve a vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges 'standing' from a ברייתא where רבן גמליאל got off his donkey, wrapped himself, and sat before dissolving a vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Standing? But it was taught: רבן גמליאל got down from the donkey, wrapped himself, sat, and dissolved his vow for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether a vow can really be dissolved while standing, since רבן גמליאל went to the trouble of sitting down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If standing were fine, why would רבן גמליאל get off his donkey and sit like a judge? His actions suggest sitting is required, which goes against רב נחמן's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Wrapped himself (in his cloak, like a judge)

phrases.english: Standing? But it was taught:
Rabban Gamliel got down from the donkey
and wrapped himself and sat
and dissolved his vow for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'standing' detail of רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that a vow may be dissolved standing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן גמליאל made a point of sitting, which implies sitting is needed.

steps.title: Two different approaches to opening a vow
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל needed to examine the case closely to uproot the vow, so he sat. רב נחמן's approach doesn't need that, so standing is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל holds: we open with regret. We need to uproot the vow, and he had to look into it, so he sat. But רב נחמן holds: we do not open with regret, and so even standing is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבן גמליאל and רב נחמן follow different views on how a vow is opened, which explains why one sat and the other allows standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבן גמליאל, dissolving meant truly uprooting the vow, which takes careful examination, so he sat down to think. רב נחמן doesn't follow that method, so no careful sitting examination is required. The sitting was about the process, not a basic rule that vows need a seated judge.

keyTerms.meaning: We open the vow based on regret

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two sides straight. Here רבן גמליאל holds פותחין בחרטה, so the vow must be uprooted, and he sat down to examine it. רב נחמן holds אין פותחין בחרטה, so he allows standing.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel holds: we open with regret.
We need to uproot the vow,
and he had to examine it; that is why he sat.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב נַחְמָן סָבַר: אֵין פּוֹתְחִין בַּחֲרָטָה,
phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman holds: we do not open with regret,
and so even standing is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבן גמליאל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disagreement in underlying method (מחלוקת in the approach)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל's sitting shows that sitting is always required.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן גמליאל sat only because his method needed careful examination; under רב נחמן's method, standing is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's 'standing' ruling holds. רבן גמליאל sat because of his own method of uprooting the vow, not because sitting is always required.

steps.title: רבא's report: the son of רב הונא בר אבין
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב נחמן about a scholar from ארץ ישראל who reported that the רבנן dissolved the vow of רב הונא בר אבין's son and told him to pray for mercy because he sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: See, master, this scholar who came from the West and said: The רבנן took care of the son of רב הונא בר אבין, dissolved his vow, and told him: Go and ask for mercy for yourself, because you sinned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings up a new report: the רבנן dissolved a vow and also told the person that vowing was a sin. This opens a new thread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is that even after the vow is dissolved, making it in the first place was wrong, so he needs to pray. The next steps explain why vowing counts as a sin.

keyTerms.meaning: They attended to, took care of (his case)

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Naḥman:
See, master, this one of the Sages
who came from the West and said:
phrases.notes: 'The West' is how Babylonian sages refer to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: The Sages attended to
the son of Rav Huna bar Avin,
and dissolved his vow for him
and said to him:

phrases.aramaic: זִיל וּבְעִי רַחֲמֵי עַל נַפְשָׁךְ דַּחֲטָאת.
phrases.english: Go and ask for mercy for yourself, because you sinned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: חֲזִי מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new report after the standing question is settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the vow was dissolved, the person was told to pray because vowing was itself a sin.

steps.title: רב דימי: anyone who vows is called a sinner
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רב דימי, brother of רב ספרא, explains the report: anyone who vows, even if he keeps it, is called a sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב דימי, the brother of רב ספרא, taught: Anyone who vows, even though he fulfills it, is called a sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source explaining why the רבנן said 'you sinned'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sin isn't breaking the vow. Even someone who keeps his vow perfectly is called a חוטא just for making it. This explains why the son had to pray even though his vow was properly dissolved.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתָנֵי רַב דִּימִי אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב סָפְרָא:
phrases.english: As Rav Dimi, the brother of Rav Safra, taught:
Anyone who vows,
even though he fulfills it,
is called a sinner.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנֵי רַב דִּימִי אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב סָפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 'you sinned' in רבא's report.
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן's statement that the son sinned by vowing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רב דימי: anyone who vows is called a sinner, even if he keeps it.

steps.title: רב זביד: the פסוק behind it
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד brings the פסוק 'If you refrain from vowing, there will be no sin in you', which implies that if you didn't refrain, there is sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: What is the פסוק? 'If you refrain from vowing, there will be no sin in you.' So if you did not refrain, there is sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד gives the פסוק that רב דימי's teaching is based on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says that holding back from vows means no sin. רב זביד reads the opposite side: if you did make a vow, there is sin. This gives רב דימי's teaching a source in the תורה.
steps.whatToRemember: Making a vow is called a sin even if you keep it. That is why the רבנן told רב הונא בר אבין's son to pray after his vow was dissolved.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said: What is the verse?
"But if you refrain from vowing,
there will be no sin in you,"
which implies: if you did not refrain, there is sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רב דימי's teaching.
steps.raayaObject: רב דימי's teaching that one who vows is a sinner.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 23:23, read in reverse: not refraining from vows means there is sin.

steps.title: Which husband statements do nothing and which confirm the vow
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that saying 'I don't want you to make any vows' or 'this is not a vow' does nothing. Saying 'you did well' or similar praise confirms the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: If a man says to his wife, 'Any vows you will make, I don't want you to make them,' or says 'This is not a vow,' he has said nothing. If he says 'You did well,' 'There is no one like you,' or 'If you hadn't vowed, I would make you vow,' his words stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the exact words a husband uses when he responds to his wife's vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some phrases do not work as cancellation. 'I don't want you to vow' speaks about vows that don't exist yet, and 'this is not a vow' is not a cancelling formula. Words of approval, though, count as confirming the vow, so he can no longer cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: He said nothing, so his words have no effect
His words stand, so the vow is confirmed

steps.confusionAlert: 'His words stand' does not mean the vow is cancelled. It means his approval counts and the vow is now locked in.

phrases.english: It was taught: One who says to his wife
'Any vows that you will vow, I don't want you to vow,'
or 'This is not a vow' —
he has not said anything.
'You did well,' and 'There is none like you,'
and 'If you had not vowed, I would make you vow' —
his words stand.
phrases.notes: His words of approval confirm her vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of the sin of vowing to a new ברייתא about a husband's wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Speaking about future vows, or saying 'this is not a vow,' does nothing. Words of approval confirm the vow.

steps.title: How a husband cancels his wife's vow on שבת
steps.stepSummary: On שבת the husband does not say 'it is cancelled for you' the way he would on a weekday. Instead he says 'take and eat' or 'take and drink,' and the vow is cancelled by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man should not say to his wife on שבת 'It is cancelled for you' or 'It is void for you' the way he says it on a weekday. Instead he tells her 'Take and eat' or 'Take and drink,' and the vow is cancelled by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא teaches that a husband can still cancel his wife's vow on שבת, but he uses different words than he would on a weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a weekday he uses the standard cancelling words. On שבת he changes the wording and simply tells her to eat or drink what she had forbidden herself. The cancellation still works, so only the way he does it changes.

keyTerms.meaning: It is cancelled for you, the husband's standard wording

phrases.english: A person should not say to his wife on Shabbat
'It is cancelled for you,' 'It is void for you,'
the way he says to her on a weekday,
rather, he says to her:
'Take and eat,' 'Take and drink,'
and the vow is cancelled by itself.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Continuation of the ברייתא in step 8
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the husband's wording, now applied to שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת a husband cancels a vow by telling her 'take and eat' or 'take and drink,' not with the weekday formula.

steps.title: He must also cancel the vow in his heart
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds that saying 'take and eat' is not enough by itself. The husband must also intend in his heart to cancel the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: And he must cancel it in his heart.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a condition to the שבת rule in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'the vow is cancelled by itself,' which could sound automatic. רבי יוחנן clarifies that the words 'take and eat' only work together with a real inner decision to cancel the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: That he cancel it in his heart, meaning with real intent

steps.confusionAlert: 'Cancelled by itself' does not mean it happens without the husband intending it. רבי יוחנן says his inner intent is required.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
And he must cancel it in his heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְצָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּבַטֵּל בְּלִבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the ברייתא's phrase 'the vow is cancelled by itself.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שבת wording only works if the husband also cancels the vow in his heart.

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל on cancelling in the heart
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that cancelling in the heart is a known idea. בית שמאי say it works only on שבת and that on a weekday he must say it out loud. בית הלל say cancelling in the heart is enough on any day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: בית שמאי say that on שבת he cancels in his heart, and on a weekday he says it with his lips. בית הלל say that either way he cancels in his heart and doesn't need to say it with his lips.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי יוחנן's idea of cancelling 'in the heart' and shows a מחלוקת about how far it goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that on שבת cancelling in the heart works, which fits רבי יוחנן. They argue about weekdays: בית שמאי require spoken words, while בית הלל say the heart alone is enough every day.

keyTerms.meaning: He says it out loud with his lips
Both this and that, here meaning both שבת and weekday

steps.whatToRemember: According to בית הלל, a husband can cancel his wife's vow in his heart alone, on שבת or a weekday.

phrases.english: It was taught: Beit Shammai say:
On Shabbat he cancels in his heart,
on a weekday he says it with his lips.
And Beit Hillel say:
Both this and that —
phrases.notes: He means both שבת and a weekday.

phrases.english: he cancels in his heart,
and he does not need to say it with his lips.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's idea of cancelling in the heart and adds a מחלוקת about weekdays.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's statement that cancelling in the heart counts
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording בית שמאי and בית הלל, who both accept cancelling in the heart on שבת

steps.title: A חכם and a husband cannot swap each other's wording
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a חכם who uses the husband's cancelling words, or a husband who uses the חכם's releasing words, has done nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: A חכם who spoke in a husband's language, or a husband who spoke in a חכם's language, has said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a new rule: each person who can remove a vow must use his own type of wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חכם releases a vow, and a husband cancels a vow. These are two different powers, each with its own words. If either one borrows the other's wording, the vow stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: A תורה scholar who can release a person from a vow
Husband, who can cancel his wife's vow
In the language, meaning the wording of

steps.confusionAlert: Both remove a vow, but they are not the same act. The חכם releases the vow and the husband cancels it, so their words cannot be swapped.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that releasing a vow and cancelling a vow are two separate powers, each with its own fixed wording.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A sage who spoke in the language of a husband,
phrases.notes: For example, the חכם said 'it is cancelled' instead of 'it is released.'

phrases.english: or a husband who spoke in the language of a sage —
has not said anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: חָכָם שֶׁאָמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן בַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new rule about wording, this time comparing the חכם and the husband.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חכם must use releasing language and a husband must use cancelling language. Swapping them has no effect.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a חכם releases vows, a husband does not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "זה הדבר" that a חכם can release a vow but a husband cannot. This supports רבי יוחנן's rule that the two roles stay separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "This is the thing" means the חכם releases vows, but a husband does not release them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבי יוחנן's rule that a husband cannot use the חכם's kind of releasing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said a husband who uses the חכם's words does nothing. The ברייתא gives the source: the words "זה הדבר" teach that releasing (התרה) belongs only to the חכם, not to the husband. So each one has his own power, and they cannot swap.

keyTerms.meaning: "This is the thing", words from the פסוק about vows
Releases a vow, the חכם's power (התרה)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יוחנן's rule comes from a פסוק and is not just his own reasoning.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: "This is the thing"
the חכם releases a vow,
but a husband does not release it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ברייתא source for רבי יוחנן's rule in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that a husband who uses the חכם's releasing language has done nothing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא learning from "זה הדבר" that only a חכם releases vows, not a husband.

steps.title: Why a פסוק is needed: a קל וחומר would let the husband release
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that without the פסוק, a קל וחומר would suggest a husband can release. A חכם cannot cancel but can release, so a husband who can cancel should surely be able to release. The ברייתא then begins "תלמוד לומר" to bring the פסוק that blocks this.
steps.simpleTranslation: For one might have thought: a חכם, who cannot cancel, can still release. So a husband, who can cancel, is it not logical that he can also release? Therefore the פסוק teaches:
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, it raises a logical argument for why a husband should be able to release vows. This sets up the next move: "תלמוד לומר" introduces the פסוק that rejects that argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is a קל וחומר: the חכם has less power (no הפרה) yet still has התרה, so the husband, who has more power (הפרה), should have התרה too. The ברייתא raises this only to show that the words "זה הדבר" are needed to stop it. The answer from the פסוק comes right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancels a vow, the husband's power (הפרה)
Is it not logical? This introduces a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up מֵפֵר and מַתִּיר. מֵפֵר means cancel, the husband's power. מַתִּיר means release, the חכם's power. The whole argument depends on keeping them apart.

phrases.english: For one might have thought:
Just as a חכם, who cannot cancel a vow,
can still release it, then a husband, who can cancel,
is it not logical that he can also release?
Therefore the פסוק teaches:

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁיָּכוֹל: וּמָה חָכָם שֶׁאֵין מֵפֵר מַתִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא's derivation in step 13 is needed by raising the קל וחומר it blocks.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that only a חכם, and not a husband, can release vows.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: the חכם, who lacks הפרה, still has התרה, so the husband, who has הפרה, should surely have התרה.
